st: Bring [[3 cups]] of the water to a boil in a heavy pot over medium-high heat.
Whisk [[0.5 cup]] of the cornmeal with the remaining [[1 cup]] cold water in a bowl until smooth and thin.
Pour the paste into the boiling water, stirring. Cook for 5 minutes until it makes a thin, glossy porridge.
Add the salt if using. Cover and cook on low heat for 5 minutes.
Add the remaining cornmeal a handful at a time, stirring firmly after each, and keep the lumps out.
Stir and press the sadza against the side of the pot for 5 minutes until it is stiff and smooth.
Cover and steam on very low heat for 5 minutes.
Shape into a smooth mound in a wet bowl. Serve hot, breaking off pieces to roll into balls and scoop up the stew.
Pat the beef dry and season with the salt and pepper.
Heat the oil in a large heavy pot over medium-high heat. Brown the beef in two batches, about 8 minutes each, and set aside.
Lower the heat and cook the onions for 7 minutes until soft and golden. Add the garlic and curry powder for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes and cook for 8 minutes until they break down into a thick sauce.
Return the beef to the pot and add the water.
Bring to a boil, then cover and simmer on low for 1 hour 15 minutes until the beef is tender.
Add the carrots if using and cook for 15 minutes more.
Uncover and simmer for 10 minutes to thicken the gravy. Taste for salt.
Serve hot with sadza and a little extra sauce.
Wash the collard greens well and slice them into thin ribbons.
Heat the oil in a large pot over medium heat. Cook the onion for 5 minutes until soft.
Add the tomatoes and cook for 6 minutes until soft and saucy.
Add the collard greens, [[0.5 cup]] of the water and the salt. Cover and cook for 15 minutes, stirring now and then, until the greens are tender.
Whisk the peanut butter with the remaining [[0.5 cup]] water in a small bowl until smooth.
Pour the peanut mixture into the greens and stir well.
Simmer uncovered on low heat for 5 minutes until the sauce thickens and coats the greens.
Taste for salt and serve hot with sadza.
Season the chicken with [[0.5 tsp]] of the salt and the pepper.
Heat the oil in a large pot over medium-high heat. Brown the chicken for about 4 minutes per side and set aside.
Lower the heat. Cook the onion for 5 minutes until soft, then add the garlic for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes and cook for 6 minutes until they break down.
Return the chicken to the pot with [[1.5 cups]] of the water. Cover and simmer on low for 25 minutes.
Whisk the peanut butter with the remaining [[0.5 cup]] water and the remaining [[0.75 tsp]] salt until smooth. Stir it into the pot.
Simmer for 15 minutes, stirring now and then, until the chicken reaches 165°F (74°C) and the sauce is thick.
Stir in the spinach and cook for 3 minutes until wilted.
Serve hot with sadza and a little extra sauce.
Rinse the dried fish in cold water to remove grit. Soak in [[1 cup]] warm water for 10 minutes, then drain and pat dry.
Heat [[2 tbsp]] of the oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Fry the fish in a single layer, about 3 minutes per side, until crisp and golden. Set aside on paper towels.
Heat the remaining [[2 tbsp]] oil in the same pan over medium heat. Cook the onion for 5 minutes until soft.
Add the garlic and cook for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes, salt and pepper and cook for 8 minutes into a thick sauce.
Return the fish to the pan, toss gently and cook for 3 minutes.
Serve hot with sadza and a little extra sauce.
Rinse the dried caterpillars well in cold water, then soak them in [[2 cups]] warm water for 30 minutes to soften.
Drain and boil them in [[1 cup]] fresh water with a pinch of salt for 10 minutes. Drain and pat dry.
Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Cook the onion for 5 minutes until golden.
Add the caterpillars and fry for 6 minutes, stirring often, until browned and a little crisp.
Add the tomatoes, the remaining salt and the chili powder if using.
Cook for 8 minutes, stirring now and then, until the tomatoes are thick and cling to the worms.
Taste and adjust the salt. Serve hot with sadza.
